description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p27-wantarray-sort.pl.

ROW BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 1 row):
  sort.t 26 `redefinition should not take effect during the sort`
  -- perl-tests/sort.t:220-226

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl) -- it DOES reproduce standalone, which
`docs/blessed-fails-review-s464.md` 1c had recorded as "does NOT reproduce in
isolation (two shapes probed); an in-file interaction".  The shape that
reproduces it needs the SELF-REDEFINING body, not just a redefinition:
    package main;
    sub Backwards_other { $b <=> $a }
    our ($a, $b); our @b;
    { no warnings 'redefine';
      *twoface = sub { *twoface = *Backwards_other; $a <=> $b }; }
    eval { @b = sort twoface 4,1,9,5 };
    print "err=[$@] b=[@b]\n";
  perl: err=[] b=[1 4 5 9]
  PCL : err=[] b=[9 5 1 4]

MECHANISM: perl resolves the comparator ONCE, when the sort op starts, and
holds the CV for the whole sort; a glob assignment made from inside the
comparator therefore cannot change the ordering of the sort in progress.
PCL re-resolves the name per comparison, so the FIRST call installs
`Backwards_other` and every later comparison uses it -- the list comes out
reverse-sorted, with no error.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: `sort.t "in-file interaction only -- does not
reproduce in isolation (review s464 1c)"` -- superseded by the reproducer
above.

FAMILY: `sort` comparator resolution.  Related but distinct: #1021
(overloaded `cmp` in the default comparator), #684 (match variables are
block-scoped in a comparator), `docs/not-supported.md` "`sort` comparator
`$a`/`$b` re-homing after an inline `package` switch".
subject: SILENT WRONG (sort): a comparator that REDEFINES ITSELF takes effect during the running sort -- `sort twoface 4,1,9,5` with `*twoface = sub { *twoface = *Backwards_other; $a <=> $b }` is `1 4 5 9` in perl and `9 5 1 4` in PCL
